Le Togo porte à l’ONU l’initiative « Correct The Map » pour une carte du monde plus fidèle à la taille réelle de l’Afrique

Unknown Equal Earth, Mercator, Africa, cartographic justice, UN
Read the source article

Quick summary

Togo is taking the African Union’s “Correct The Map” campaign to the UN, turning projection choice into a debate about symbolic justice and global representation.

Key takeaways

  • Tchad Infos reports that Togo, acting on behalf of the African Union, plans to bring the “Correct The Map” initiative to the United Nations in an effort to move international institutions away from the Mercator projection and toward Equal Earth.
  • At the heart of the argument is a familiar critique of Mercator.
  • What makes the story notable is its institutional ambition.
  • The article also uses the language of “justice cognitive,” which signals that map design is being interpreted as part of a broader postcolonial struggle over knowledge representation.
  • For mapping and cartographic culture, the initiative is important because it shows that debates over projections remain alive even in an age dominated by interactive digital maps.
